title: Regular coefficient data with division and Jacobian conditions
statement:
Let $X\hookrightarrow M$ be a reduced closed subscheme of a smooth scheme of finite type over a characteristic-zero field $k$ [def-pc-reduced-scheme] [def-weil-closed-immersion] [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. At any point $a$, etale-locally after shrinking, there exist a smooth closed $N\subset M$, coordinates $w$ on $N$, formal transverse coordinates $Z$, a finite diagram $D=V+\mathbf N^n$, and formal generators
$$f_i(W,Z)=\sum_\gamma c_{i\gamma}(W)Z^\gamma$$
of the Taylor ideal of $X$ at $a$. Each coefficient is the Taylor expansion of a regular function $c_{i\gamma}$ on $N$. The transverse variables $Z$ are precisely the variables occurring to positive power in the vertex monomials; the vertices have zero $W$ components. Write the ordered vertices as $\alpha_i$, $d_i=|\alpha_i|$, and partition $D$ into disjoint sets $\alpha_i+\Delta_i$ by assigning each exponent to its first vertex. The data satisfy the following conditions, also after Taylor expansion at every point of the coefficient order locus $\{x\in N:\operatorname{ord}_x c_{i\gamma}\ge d_i-|\gamma|\ (|\gamma|<d_i)\}$:
(1) $\operatorname{ord} f_i=d_i$.
(2) For every degree bound $q$, the homogeneous polynomials have unique division by the initial forms of the $f_i$ with $d_i\le q$, quotients supported in $\Delta_i$, and remainder supported outside the diagram generated by those vertices.
(3) Every element $f$ of the Taylor ideal has an expansion $f=\sum q_i f_i$ with $\operatorname{supp}q_i\subset\Delta_i$.
(4) Group the vertices into blocks of equal total degree, and let $Z^\ell$ be the variables occurring in the first $\ell$ blocks. For each such variable $Z_j$, choose $\alpha_{i(j)}=\beta_j+e_j$ in those blocks. The derivatives $g_j=\partial_Z^{\beta_j}f_{i(j)}$ belong to $(Z^\ell)$ and their Jacobian in the variables of $Z^\ell$ is invertible at the point.
(5) For any fixed $Q\ge\max d_i-1$, the generators in later blocks satisfy $\partial_{Z^\ell}^{\beta}f_i\in(Z^\ell)$ for $|\beta|\le Q$ lying in the diagram of the first $\ell$ blocks, restricted to its essential variables.
The subscheme $N$ is cut out by regular equations with the invertible Jacobians in (4). The coefficient functions and these equations are defined on one common etale neighbourhood. One can shrink so that the extended Hilbert--Samuel function throughout it is at most its value at $a$. Order means containment in powers of the local maximal ideal, with infinite order for zero. The number of eliminated variables may be zero. This is existence of specially chosen division-adapted generators; it does not assert algebraization of an arbitrary formal standard basis.

source.place: VIII 2.3.11--2.3.13, pp.93--94; detailed local input: Bierstone--Milman, Invent. Math. 128 (1997), 207--302, conditions (7.1)--(7.2), Theorem 9.6 and its block induction (9.7)--(9.14); Bierstone--Milman--Temkin, arXiv:0905.3580, section 6.2. No Stacks tag states this algebraization theorem.

proof.text: Apply [lem-per-nonreduced-regular-hilbert-coefficients] to the same closed immersion and structure morphism. It requires no reducedness assumption and supplies m, n, s and ordered vertices alpha before the choice of Q. Retain its orderedVertices conclusion. For each allowed Q, take its regular coefficient datum and forget the extra positive-degree and zero-Taylor-ideal conclusions. This is precisely the required datum, including all five formal conditions and the pointwise extended Hilbert bound. No coordinates, ideals, or hypotheses are changed. Empty vertex lists and zero eliminated variables are included by the same theorem.

The item statement is byte-identical to side-live; only proof, proof_deps, proof_origin and split_report changed. The item is not on the drop list and no SGA is used. The old 13 steps are all moved, none summarised: steps 2-4 go to block-straightening-projection-transport, 5-7 to exact-block-coefficient-projection, 8 and 12 to the formal-division node, 9-10 to coefficient-locus-uniform-division, 11 to coefficient-order-hilbert-equality, 13 to extended-hilbert-local-upper-bound. The new nodes are of comparable size. Every statement was checked by hand. Block straightening: h_j(a)=0, the y-Jacobian is triangular because beta_j+e_k for k>j is deg-lex earlier than the vertex, and the shift y=phi(W)+Y moves exponent onto W, which comes first, so first exponents are kept. P is transported through the Taylor homomorphism c -> sum d_y^delta c|_C/delta! Y^delta. Projection: B(a) is unitriangular, v(P_l H)=0, and the corrections have distinct transverse exponents. Uniform division: restricted determinants up to b(D_l) with lift by complementary degree. Equality: (g_j)=(Z) gives the ideal (Z, d_W^delta c_igamma), whose zero set is S. Local bound: Fitting opens plus one witness degree per pointwise-bad function, which correctly repairs the old lexicographic-only step 13 that the S2 reviewer had flagged. Edge cases checked: s=0, n=0, E empty, l=1 with P=1, arbitrary Q; the NA counterexample still gives f3=x^4. Three repairable faults, all repaired. (1) E1/C4: exact-block-coefficient-projection assumed first exponents (0,alpha_i) for all i, but later vertices use variables that are still coordinates w at block l, so the node did not apply to the induction. The statement is restated: alpha_i is read in (W,T), and is (0,alpha_i) only for i<=s_l. (2) C3: old step 3 used an 'unchanged initial diagram' of K_a that no cited statement gives. It is now cited via lem-trf-jet-diagram-hilbert-control (H_{K_a}=H_D in the step-1 chart, invariant under the straightenings) plus the division node. (3) C5: the new lem-trf-diagram-supported-formal-division duplicates the existing Q69 lem-trf-homogeneous-continuous-formal-division (same basis hypothesis, unique supported division, and H_I=H_D iff r=0 on I); its other clauses are elementary or come from uniform division at b=a. It is dropped and its uses are re-cited. The assembly is reordered: uniform division now comes before the steps at a and at b in S. It is now 2745 characters. Fixes are in fixes/dag/nodes/sec-trace-formula/{lem-trf-regular-hilbert-coefficient-data,lem-trf-exact-block-coefficient-projection}.json. reviewed_lean.note: H3 in new def RegularHilbertCoefficientDatum.first_minimal: Finsupp.DegLex (·<·)(·<·) on Fin m ⊕ Fin n uses Mathlib's Sum.instLTSum (LiftRel, W and Z incomparable), so Pi.Lex ignores the W part against the vertex (0,α) and forces W-monomial coefficients to vanish.
